newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer, watches Dow, dollar.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer, watches Dow, dollar.

text.p: Dealers were looking for gold to push a little higher on Wednesday after an overnight bounce from the lows on a fall in the Dow and U.S. dollar.
"But medium term we are still looking to the downside," a dealer said.
Gold was fixed $3.00 firmer at $370.40 after it fixed on Tuesday afternoon at its lowest level since November 3, 1993.
A late fall on the New York Stock Exchange as investors took profits on Tuesday and a weaker dollar against several of the major currencies encouraged investors to seek safety in gold.
The Dow Jones Industrial average was off 79 points.
It was the biggest one-day fall since July 15 and widely forecast after the Dow had soared 500 points or eight percent during November.

"There is a possibility of the Dow trying lower again today. The Dow and the dollar are the keys things for gold today," one dealer said, adding that trading on these issues would be largely intraday.
Investment fund buying was cited as spurring the overnight rally which brought in short covering from the professionals.
Covering early in Europe took gold through $370.00 where stops were hit taking it to the day's high at $370.80 bid.
"It might try higher again later," a dealer said.
Nevertheless, the outlook for gold remained bleak with the current uptick seen as no more than a correction in an severely oversold market and an opportunity for profit taking.

Dealers said producer selling was likely to continue to put pressure on prices as the miners sought to protect their income. The impact of falling gold prices had been made the more adverse by movements in their local currencies against the dollar.
Persistent talk of a central bank gold sale within the past month or so also weighed on the market, dealers said.
The other metals were also firmer behind gold although dealers said business was very quiet and largely confined to the professionals.
"It probably helped gold on Tuesday that the rest of the complex managed to hold their ground. If they had slipped, gold would have been down to $365," a dealer said.
Silver was marked up nine cents from Tuesday's close to $4.79/$4.81 although not much business was being done.
Platinum and palladium were both very quiet. Platinum was indicated at $373.25/$374.25 up $2.75 and palladium was a dollar firmer at $115.25/$116.25.
